title: SQL: create, insert, update
summary: Make a table, add rows, change them safely with WHERE, and the upsert that does both.

text: CREATE TABLE gives a table its name and its columns, each with a type.
- sqlite3 movies.db creates the file as soon as you write something in it.
- .schema shows how a table was made: handy to check your columns.
$ sqlite3 movies.db "CREATE TABLE movies (title TEXT, year INTEGER);"
INSERT INTO adds a row. Name the columns, then give the values in the same order.
- Text goes between single quotes: 'Alien'. Numbers don't.
- A column you leave out gets NULL, the empty value (or its default, if it has one).
UPDATE changes rows; WHERE picks which ones.
- Forget WHERE and every row changes: a classic accident in production.
- Run a SELECT with the same WHERE first: you see exactly what you're about to change.
- DELETE FROM works the same way, and needs the same care.
An upsert inserts a row, or updates it when it's already there.
- ON CONFLICT needs a column that can't repeat, like a PRIMARY KEY: item, here.
- excluded.qty is the value you tried to insert: 3.
- INSERT OR REPLACE is different: it deletes the old row first, so its other columns are lost.
